result:
The proposed answer π is incorrect; the minimum fractional revival time is t* = 2π/p.

**Graph structure.** In Z_{2p}, x ~ y exactly when x − y is odd and not divisible by p. Each even vertex is therefore adjacent to every odd vertex except its antipode x + p. So X is K_{p,p} minus a perfect matching, where the matching pairs each vertex with its antipode.

**Spectral form.** Order the vertices so that each antipodal pair has the same index in the two parts. Then A = σ_x ⊗ B with B = J − I, where J is the all-ones matrix. B has eigenvalue p − 1 on the all-ones vector and −1 on its orthogonal complement. This gives

U(t) = I ⊗ cos(tB) − i σ_x ⊗ sin(tB).

The two blocks are

- cos(tB) = cos t · I + (cos((p−1)t) − cos t) J/p,
- sin(tB) = −sin t · I + (sin((p−1)t) + sin t) J/p.

**Fractional revival between a and its antipode.** We need U(t)e_a to be supported only on e_a and e_{a'}. The off-diagonal entries of both blocks must therefore vanish:

- cos((p−1)t) = cos t,
- sin((p−1)t) = −sin t.

Together these say e^{i(p−1)t} = e^{−it}, that is, e^{ipt} = 1. So t = 2πk/p for an integer k.

**Minimal time.** The smallest positive solution is t = 2π/p. At this time the antipodal amplitude is −i·(−sin t) = i sin(2π/p), which is nonzero because p is odd. So this is genuine fractional revival, not just a return to the starting vertex.

**Check with p = 3.** Here X = C₆ and the time is 2π/3, consistent with the formula.

The proposed solution's value of π does not match, and its argument is not a real derivation.

VERDICT: REJECT
